title: fix(messaging): the one-time digest conversion rewrites only rows that held none before its claim

## 维护者速读

- 用户无感的升级修补:升级当天那次「把旧的不汇总清成未设置」只改开始前已存在的那批记录,运行期间成员新选的「不汇总」原样保留。
- 属于「成员不汇总与免打扰优先于组织默认」那项修复的收尾,替运行期间改了设置的成员解决选择被清掉的问题。
- 出错时,升级运行那几秒里选了「不汇总」的成员会被改回跟随组织;可直接撤回本改动,回到原先的做法。
- 无。

## What changes

`packages/services/service-messaging/src/preference-digest-conversion.ts` (the one-time conversion of the legacy digest `none` to empty, ruling 7073270426 on #35123, item 4):

- **Snapshot before the claim.** The pass reads the ids (and organization) of every row holding `digest = 'none'` first, in pages by id cursor (`id > last`, `orderBy id asc`, page size 10000), then claims its `sys_migration` row, then rewrites exactly that snapshot with the same compare-and-set as before (`where: { id, digest: 'none' }`, the row's own organization threaded).
- **No re-read.** The loop that re-read `where: { digest: 'none' }` after each batch (and the `seen` set that ended it) is gone, and so is its "re-reading failed after the claim" branch: a failure on any page of the snapshot now happens before the claim and answers `read-failed`, so the next boot retries with nothing recorded.
- An optional third parameter `{ pageSize }` (module-internal; the function is not exported from the package entry) lets the pin exercise more than one page.

Ruling text relied on (item 4):

> ⛔ The conversion must not run again after the fix is live: from then on `none` is a member's real choice.

The deployment serves while the boot hook runs, so a `none` written during the pass is written under the fixed release.

### Read first (by risk)

1. `preference-digest-conversion.ts` — `readSnapshot` (cursor paging; the missing-table answer applies to the first page only) and the rewrite loop that now iterates the snapshot once.
2. `preference-digest-three-states.integration.test.ts` — `interceptOnce` and the "a none written during the pass" pin.
3. `.changeset/36369-digest-conversion-snapshot.md`.

## Tests

New pins in `preference-digest-three-states.integration.test.ts` (real `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver` better-sqlite3 file database that an earlier release created):

- a `none` written during the pass (a new row with an explicit `none`, and a `daily` row switched to `none`) survives it; only the pre-claim row is rewritten (`converted: 1`);
- the snapshot is read in pages by id: five legacy rows across two organizations with `pageSize: 2` are all converted;
- a claim that fails after the read (ledger insert refused) answers `claim-failed`, logs one error, rewrites nothing and leaves no ledger row;
- another node claiming between the read and the claim answers `already-run` and this pass rewrites nothing.

All readings at head `6bd074ce`, after `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/service-messaging^...' build` (lock VERDICT command-exit 0).

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-messaging test`: Test Files 80 passed (80), Tests 1088 passed (1088).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-messaging typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.scripts.json`): exit 0.
- Both under `os-verify-lock.sh`: VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `test:repo` not run locally (diff does not touch that project); CI `Test Core` runs it.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (one-shot, through scripts/ablation-replace.mjs; the test imports the module from source, so no dist leg)</summary>

1. Re-read reintroduced: the snapshot loop replaced by a generator that re-reads `digest = 'none'` after the snapshot and yields ids not yet seen (the pre-fix shape). Mutation landed (anchor 1 to 0, blob 7ad5cf7fdbdf to cfc30aecaf87). Result: "a none written during the pass is not rewritten" FAILED, `converted` expected 1, received 3; Tests 1 failed, 8 passed. Restored: blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
2. One page only: the short-page test before `return snapshot;` deleted, so the read stops after the first page. Result: "reads the snapshot in pages by id" FAILED, `converted` expected 5, received 2; Tests 1 failed, 8 passed. Restored: blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **Split off — seat decides:** the Notification Settings page has no "follow the organization again" action for digest or quiet hours (optional item 1 of the card).
- **Split off — seat decides:** `QUIET_HOURS_OFF` is spelled in both `preference-resolver.ts` and the UI `myPreferences.ts` with no pin tying them together (optional item 2 of the card).
- **What the snapshot does not close (by construction).** When the claim fails, nothing is rewritten and nothing can be recorded (the ledger is the thing that failed), so the next boot takes a new snapshot and a `none` written between those two boots is converted with the rest. The card reads the snapshot as covering this case; it covers the claim-fails-after-the-read case only within one boot (pinned above). The failure is logged at `error` naming the fix. A row that held the legacy `none` in the snapshot and is re-set to `none` by its member before its own rewrite is indistinguishable from the legacy value and is converted; that window is the time between the snapshot and that row's update.

## Verification

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-messaging exec vitest run src/preference-digest-three-states.integration.test.ts` — expect 9 passed, including "a none written during the pass is not rewritten: only the rows read before the claim are".
